title: Unresponsive-service triage trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for service-stopped-responding trace events: one outage where a live service stops answering — the outside-in probes and the failure mode they classify, the evidence a restart would have destroyed, the thread dump grouped by top frame, the bounded pools, the saturation arithmetic, and the stopwatch.

service.description: The service that stopped responding, e.g. payments-api.

symptom.description: The symptom as it was reported or alerted, before any of it is a measurement.

stage.description: Technical lifecycle state of the triage, translated by the visualizer.

failureMode.description: Which kind of 'not responding' this is; derived from the probes by classify(). 'unknown' until classified.

minutes.description: Minutes charged since the alarm; every action has a fixed deterministic cost.

processRestarted.description: True once the hung process has been replaced; after that no artifact can be captured from it.

probes.description: The outside-in probes, ordered by layer rather than by when they were run.

layer.description: Which layer was probed, outermost first; 'inside' is the same call from inside the container against localhost.

command.description: The exact command that was run, e.g. 'nc -vz payments-api.internal 8080'.

outcome.description: What the layer answered; 'partial' means some instances answer and some do not.

detail.description: The exact answer, e.g. 'Connection refused' or '200 UP in 4ms'.

evidence.description: Artifacts that only exist while the process is still hung, in the order they were taken.

artifact.description: What was captured, e.g. '3 thread dumps, 5 seconds apart'.

lost.description: True when the capture was attempted after the process had already been replaced.

threads.description: The thread dump collapsed into groups by top frame — the way a dump is actually read.

count.description: How many threads share this top frame.

state.description: The java.lang.Thread.State reported for the group.

frame.description: The top frame the group is parked at, plus what it is waiting for.

share.description: Percentage of all dumped threads recorded so far; the biggest share is the outage.

threadTotal.description: Total threads across all recorded groups.

pools.description: Bounded things a request queues for, in the order they were read.

name.description: The pool, e.g. 'the Tomcat worker pool'.

queued.description: Requests waiting for a slot; 100% used with nobody waiting is a well-sized pool.

saturated.description: True when inUse has reached max.

gc.description: The garbage collector reading; absent until it is read.

pausePercent.description: Share of wall clock spent in GC pauses.

heapAfterGcPercent.description: How full the heap still is immediately after a full collection — the number that matters.

thrashing.description: True when pauses dominate and the heap stays full: alive, busy, answering nobody.

resources.description: Readings below the application — CPU quota, descriptors, disk, node — which never appear in a stack trace.

name.description: What was read, e.g. 'open file descriptors'.

alarming.description: Whether the reading is a suspect.

deadlock.description: The JVM's own deadlock verdict; absent unless the dump printed one.

monitors.description: The monitors each holds and needs.

capacity.description: Little's law applied to the worker pool; absent until computed.

serviceMillis.description: How long one request occupies a worker.

capacityPerSecond.description: threads / service time — what the pool can actually complete per second.

deficitPerSecond.description: Arrival minus capacity: how fast the queue grows.

exhaustMillis.description: How long it takes arriving traffic to occupy every worker.

overloaded.description: True when arrivals exceed capacity, so the queue grows without bound.

mitigation.description: The action that restored service; absent while users are still down.

action.description: The reversible action taken, e.g. a rollback or a feature flag.

effect.description: What it did for traffic — and what it cost in evidence.

rootCause.description: The confirmed cause, or null while nothing explains both the symptom and the timing.

causeEvidence.description: The reading that made the cause more than a story.

fix.description: The change that was shipped; absent while nothing has been changed.

blind.description: True when it shipped with no confirmed cause — usually disguised as raising a limit.

verified.description: Whether the re-run of the failing check passed; null until it is run.

guards.description: The alerts, timeouts, probes and scripts left behind — the only permanent output of an outage.

missteps.description: Triage errors recorded as consequences of the order actions were taken in.
